== Research notes (October 2026) ==
'''Build notes:''' Added his 1999 and 2000 Star Trek CCG World Championship results, his 2000 Worlds deck "Familiar Faces" and his Team Hyperlight listing, all from Decipher's archived pages (Wayback captures opened and checked). The deck is summarised in prose; the full list is on the cited Decipher page. No Star Trek decklist page was created, because the decklist templates (Side, CardLink) are for SWCCG cards.

'''Missing data:''' No record found of him playing Star Wars CCG. Searched: every archived DecipherCon 1999 page (photos, schedules, all event score sheets), every archived DecipherCon 2000 page, Decipher's 1999 and 2000 Star Wars finalist lists, the wiki, and the VPS snapshot corpus. No 1999 Worlds deck found (Decipher's archived Star Trek deck designs only cover the 2000 finalists). The DecipherCon 1999 photo caption "looks like a winner" refers to no posted result.

'''Possibly faulty data:''' Decipher gave three hometowns: Coquitlam, BC (1999 finalists list and photo caption), Burnaby, BC (2000 qualifier and finalist lists) and Kamloops, BC (2000 semifinalist list). The lead keeps Coquitlam from the 1999 sources.

'''Marginal cuts:''' The trekcc.org designer James Monsebroten ("Orbin"), lead designer of several Continuing Committee First Edition virtual sets, wrote in 2022 that he played a Worlds Day 1 match "either 1999 or 2000". Not added: trekcc.org returns 520 to Wayback saves, so it needs a swccg.com snapshot first. [[User:Comlink Cursor|Comlink Cursor]] ([[User talk:Comlink Cursor|talk]]) 02:11, 26 October 2026 (UTC)
